title: A-linear degree-zero lift of the finite adjunction counit
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] between Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $A=f_*\mathcal O_X$ finite locally free [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and $L$ invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume derived categories of module sheaves on X and Y exist [def-pc-derived-category]. Fix $R:D_{QCoh}(X)\to D_{QCoh}(Y)$, its comparison with $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and an adjunction $R\dashv a$. Fix $K\cong L[0]$, a quasi-coherent module $M$ on X, an isomorphism $e_0:M[0]\cong a(K)$, and the canonical comparison $c:(f_*M)[0]\cong Rf_*(M[0])$ given by the inverse single-complex comparison followed by the right-derived unit. Let $T$ be scalar restriction along $\mathcal O_Y\to A$ and $g:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,A)$ [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. Fix an exact functor $H:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, a natural isomorphism $HT\cong\mathcal Hom(A,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and an adjunction $T\dashv H$. There exists an A-linear isomorphism $j:g_*M\cong H(L)$ such that $(T(j)\mathbin{\gg}\varepsilon_{H,L})[0]$ equals $c\mathbin{\gg}Rf_*(e_0)\mathbin{\gg}\mathrm{comparison}_{aK}^{-1}\mathbin{\gg}\varepsilon_{R,K}\mathbin{\gg}e_L$. No sectionwise evaluation or multiplication-action compatibility is asserted.

proof.text: Choose the standard derived category of A-modules. Scalar restriction is exact and the supplied H is exact. Derive their adjunction using localization of the termwise functors. The derived adjunction counit formula identifies its counit, on L[0], with the single of the underived counit via the canonical exact-functor single comparisons. Additivity of H follows from being right adjoint between additive categories.

Let G = Rg_*, rho = RT and rhoR = RH, with derived adjunction adjA. Construct gamma : G ⋙ rho ≅ Rf_* from the exact-restriction comparison, the inverse derived-composite comparison, and the identity g_* ⋙ T = f_*. Put J = iX ⋙ G and beta : R ⋙ iY ≅ J ⋙ rho using comparison and gamma.symm. The finite affine derived equivalence makes J fully faithful. Since K is bounded below by eL, finite_scalar_right_adjoint_qcoh puts rhoR(K) in the essential image of J. Define phi as the adjA-transpose of beta.inv.app(a(K)) followed by iY(adj.counit.app K). For every N, composition with phi is bijective by full faithfulness of J and iY and the two adjunction hom equivalences. Choose an isomorphism J(N0) ≅ rhoR(K) from essential image membership; bijectivity supplies a right inverse to phi, and injectivity at a(K) makes it a left inverse. Thus phi is an isomorphism. Its transpose equation gives rho(phi) followed by adjA.counit = gamma.hom followed by comparison.inv followed by the geometric counit, with this same gamma.

Construct the canonical g_* single comparison using its right-derived unit. After exact scalar restriction and the same canonical gamma of step 2, its image is the canonical f_* single comparison, invertible by affine_singlePushforward_unit_isIso for the quasi-coherent M. Derived scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms: its cohomology is underived restriction, which reflects isomorphisms through the unchanged underlying abelian sheaf. Hence the g_* single comparison is invertible. Combine it, Rg_*(e0), phi, the derived image of eL, and the exact-H single comparison to obtain an isomorphism from (g_*M)[0] to H(L)[0]. Full faithfulness of singleFunctor over A lifts this isomorphism to j.

Use the same canonical gamma constructed in step 2, from g_* followed by T being identically f_*, the exact-restriction right-derived comparison, and the derived-composite comparison. Its localization factorization equations identify the composite of the canonical g_* single comparison with this factorization and exact T single comparison with the canonical f_* single comparison. Apply naturality along e0 and eL. Restrict the lifted morphism to O_Y, use the counit equation of step 2 and the derived-adjunction counit formula of step 1, then use hc to replace the initial canonical f_* single comparison by c.hom. The zero object, empty schemes, and rank-zero A satisfy the same identities.
